decisions.decision: Cell 5 spec is incompatible with macOS Sonoma+ TCC behavior — needs rewrite
decisions.rationale: macOS does not enforce TCC revoke mid-session for a running app; the OS shows a 'Quit & Reopen / Later' modal and defers enforcement until the next launch. The Cell 5 trigger (System Settings toggle) cannot produce a frame stall the FrameStallWatchdog would detect. Watchdog code itself is fine (gates on FRAME_STALL_THRESHOLD_MS; unit-tested). Suggested alternative triggers: USB camera physical unplug, scripted AVCaptureSession invalidation.

When the user clicked Recheck while still denied, the state machine emitted the same cause and CameraStatusDialog::show's D-14 duplicate-suppression silently dismissed the re-show, making the button appear broken. Fix: call cameraStatusDialog_.reset() in the editor's Action::RecheckPermission handler before cam->recheckPermission(). On still-denied path the dialog now re-displays (implicit 'still denied, no change' feedback); on now-authorized path no fallback is emitted and the camera opens normally.

decisions.decision: Captured browser-fed JTBv capture path as v1.4+ deferred idea
decisions.rationale: User raised: 'maybe at some point streaming the video via web again but using this new method with GUID matching?' Phase 14.3's RawDataSendWrite(guid[16], ..., JTBv, ...) is producer-agnostic, so a browser companion using WebCodecs/getUserMedia could feed frames into the same pipeline. Unentitled hosts (REAPER) would get camera via the browser. Strictly v1.4+ — explicitly excluded by v1.3 roadmap PASS 3 lock (no VDO.Ninja teardown, no new web stack). Saved to user memory as [[web-capture-fallback]].

advisory_constraints.name: macOS Sonoma TCC revoke is deferred-to-restart
advisory_constraints.description: When toggling camera permission OFF for a running app, macOS Sonoma+ shows a 'Quit & Reopen / Later' modal and defers actual enforcement until the next app launch. Frames continue flowing through the open AVCaptureSession. Any UAT/test that assumes a System Settings toggle will produce a mid-session frame stop is wrong. Use USB unplug, scripted session invalidation, or restart-path testing instead.

advisory_constraints.name: scripts/build.sh default target includes failing test_encryption
advisory_constraints.description: Running `./scripts/build.sh` with no args enumerates all targets in build-juce/, which includes test_encryption.cpp — a pre-existing compile failure (encrypt_payload_with_iv undeclared identifier, documented in HANDOFF.json from May 15 as deferred). The build appears to 'fail' but JUCE plugin targets may not even start linking. Workaround: pass JUCE plugin targets explicitly — `./scripts/build.sh JamWideJuce_Standalone JamWideJuce_AU JamWideJuce_VST3 JamWideJuce_CLAP`. ninja's per-target dependency graph correctly skips test_encryption since it's not a dep of those targets.
